trajectory_clusters.common_pattern: Extract values from a Treasury Bulletin table and apply simple aggregation: sum with exclusions, arithmetic mean, list extraction, or direct difference. No complex formula needed beyond basic arithmetic.
trajectory_clusters.evidence: All 7 trajectories locate a specific bulletin table (FFO-3, FD-1, CM-I-2, PDO-1, Summary of Receipts), extract values with column mapping, cross-validate, and compute a simple sum/mean/list/difference.

trajectory_clusters.common_pattern: Extract a series of values and compute a statistical measure: geometric mean, population standard deviation, mean absolute deviation, or Hazen percentile. Each requires a distinct formula with specific divisor (N vs N-1) or plotting position.
trajectory_clusters.evidence: q013 computes geometric mean of 80 monthly values via log-sum-exp; q032 computes population std dev (divide by N) of TIPS prices; q054 computes MAD of excise taxes; q055 computes Hazen 85th percentile with P_i=(i-0.5)/N.

trajectory_clusters.common_pattern: Extract time-series or paired data and fit a regression or compute correlation: OLS linear regression for prediction, Zipf exponent via log-log OLS, Pearson correlation and R-squared. Each uses explicit regression/correlation formulas with independent verification.
trajectory_clusters.evidence: q009 and q106 use OLS slope/intercept formulas for prediction; q039 fits log(size) on log(rank) for Zipf exponent; q058 computes R-squared from Pearson r; q087 computes absolute difference of Pearson r between two years; q060 fits linear regression but finds actual value unavailable (discontinued table).

trajectory_clusters.common_pattern: Extract values and apply a specific rate/transform formula: Box-Cox transform, CAGR/geometric annual rate, centered moving average, arc elasticity, realized variance, or annualized volatility. Each formula is mathematically distinct and must not be merged with others.
trajectory_clusters.evidence: q005 applies Box-Cox(y,lambda=0.75) then takes difference; q041 computes (end/start)^(1/n)-1; q048 computes 3-period centered moving average of duty rates (Oracle regression: r1 candidate merged this into generic compute and got wrong answer); q067 uses arc elasticity midpoint formula; q097 computes squared log return; q119 computes sqrt(52)*|log return|.

trajectory_clusters.common_pattern: Extract values and compute ratio, percentage, or weighted average: weighted average denomination, percent contribution change, share change with absolute change, weighted average with custom weights, absolute percent difference.
trajectory_clusters.evidence: q012 computes total value / total bills for weighted avg denomination; q047 computes (part/total*100) change between years; q071 computes share change in percentage points plus absolute change; q080 computes (v1*1+v2*2)/3; q115 computes |a-b|/base*100.

trajectory_clusters.common_pattern: Extract values in foreign currency units and convert using exchange rates from FCP tables, then compute a difference or risk measure. Requires careful handling of conversion direction and unit scale (billions vs millions).
trajectory_clusters.evidence: q024 converts JPY and GBP positions to USD using exchange rates from FCP-II-1 and FCP-IV-1, then takes absolute difference; q081 extracts mutual fund holdings, computes parametric VaR (mu - z*sigma), then converts USD loss to JPY using exchange rate.

changes.summary: New skill for Treasury Bulletin source location: publication lag rules, file naming convention, fiscal-year mapping, and table catalog routing.

New skill for data extraction, cross-validation, and computation. Contains 20+ distinct named computation procedures (geometric_mean, centered_moving_average, population_std_dev, box_cox_transform, etc.), each with its own formula and precision check. Addresses Oracle regression by keeping each computation type separate.

oracle_memory_used.action: Created separate centered_moving_average procedure with explicit 3-period formula and centering-position check, distinct from all other computation types. Avoided the r1 anti-pattern of merging CAGR, geometric mean, OLS, centered moving average, and std dev into one generic compute step.
